canonical_title: Damage tolerance for non-fracture critical components

versions.title_at_revision: Damage tolerance for non-fracture critical components
versions.text:
Standard: When operated, under steady state and transient conditions, IAW 7.3.1, non-fracture-critical engine parts resist failure caused by the presence of material, manufacturing, processing, maintenance, and service-induced defects per a damage tolerance approach covered by the MIL- STD-3024, Fracture Screening through Additively Manufactured Components paragraphs. Non-fracture-critical parts are safety-critical or mission-critical components for which LCF-driven crack growth is not a primary failure mechanism, parts that are not highly loaded, or non-structural parts. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Analysis is conducted per the damage tolerance approach covered by the MIL-STD-3024, Fracture Screening through Additively Manufactured Components paragraphs to verify damage tolerance capability. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Components are selected for verification by test (e.g., impact testing, damping testing, leak-before-burst testing, proof testing, defect characterization testing) per the damage tolerance approach covered by the MIL-STD-3024, Fracture Screening through Additively Manufactured Components paragraphs.
  (2) Lab test: Full engine durability test or AMT/ASMET is conducted in a ground-based sea level test cell IAW JSSG-2007, Appendix A, Verification section, Endurance Tests paragraph unless exempted by the damage tolerance approach covered by the MIL-STD-3024, Fracture Screening through Additively Manufactured Components paragraphs. Tests include product-representative inlet conditions and extractions, and rotor imbalance. Tests are conducted using engine control software or schedules of the type design. Post-test teardown and NDI of hardware verifies predicted damage tolerance characteristics. Minimum endurance test duration is twice the planned flight test duration. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (3) Lab test: Full engine durability test or AMT/ASMET is conducted in a ground-based sea level test cell IAW JSSG-2007, Appendix A, Verification section, Endurance Tests paragraph unless exempted by the damage tolerance approach covered by the MIL-STD-3024, Fracture Screening through Additively Manufactured Components paragraph. Tests include product-representative inlet conditions and extractions, and rotor imbalance. Tests are conducted using engine control software or schedules of the type design. Post-test teardown and NDI of hardware verifies predicted damage tolerance characteristics. Minimum endurance test duration is the scheduled depot inspection interval or half the cold part DSL.
